Heard Sri.H.R.Gundappa, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Sri.Ayush G Bhat, learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 absent.
Though notice to respondents No.3 and 4 served, have remained absent.

3. This petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. with the following prayer:
"To allow this criminal petition, by setting aside the impugned order dated 17th July 2019, passed by the 1st Additional District and Sessions Judge Court, Dharwad,
sitting at Hubballi, dismissing the Criminal Revision Petition No.78/2018, by Shri.Basheer Ahamad S/O Appalal Shaikh vs Shri.Mohammed Rafiq S/O Immasab ... on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144081512/
2 confirming the order of dismissal of private complaint, passed by the Principal Civil Judge & JMFC Court at Hubballi, in unregistered P.C. /2018 (unnumbered p.c.) by allowing this criminal petition."
4.
Brief facts of the case are as under:

The petitioner filed a private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. alleging the offence said to have committed by respondents No.1 to 4 for the offence punishable under Sections 405, 420, 463 read with 34 of IPC.
5.
The said private complaint was considered by the learned Magistrate as to whether the matter requires reference to the police under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. for investigation.

On consideration of the material on record, the learned Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Hubballi passed a detailed written order refusing to refer the matter to police and dismissed the same noting that the dispute is civil in nature.

6. Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioner herein filed a revision petition before the District Court in Crl.R.P.No.78/2018 and the learned District Judge after securing records and hearing the parties in detail, by order dated 17.07.2019 dismissed the revision petition on merits.
7. Being aggrieved by the dismissal of the revision petition, the petitioner is before this Court.

8. Sri H.R.Gundappa, learned counsel for the petitioner/ complainant vehemently contended that both the Courts have failed to appreciate the criminality alleged against respondents No.1 to 4 and wrongly dismissed the complaint of the petitioner and sought for allowing the petition.
9. In the light of the arguments put forth on behalf of the petitioner and the grounds urged in the petition, this Court perused the material on record.

10. Admittedly, a sale deed said to have been executed by accused No.3 in favour of others in respect of agriculture land bearing Sy.No.978/1 measuring 4 acres 12 guntas of Kusugal village, Hubballi,
the petitioner said to have given assistance in that regard and he was promised to sold two plots measuring 30 x 40 feet.
The said promise got breached by the accused persons and therefore private complaint is filed.
11. It is settled principles of law that mere breach of promise per se would not amount to a criminal offence as is contemplated under the provisions of Section 405, 420 and 463 r/w 34 of IPC.
Same has been rightly appreciated by the learned trial Magistrate and learned District Judge in the impugned order.

12. Given the scope of Section 482 in a matter of this nature, this court is of the considered opinion that prima facie recording of a finding by the learned trial Magistrate that the matter is of the civil nature which was confirmed by the learned District Judge does not suffer from any legal infirmity or perversity so as to interfere with the same by exercising inherent jurisdiction U/sec.482 Cr.P.C.

ORDER Admission declined, petition is dismissed.
